steps.label: Divide through by cos9°
steps.margin_note: First mark, and the move that unlocks it. Dividing top and bottom by cos9° turns every term into a tangent, and 1 is tan45°.
lines: Divide numerator and denominator by cos9°:

recall.must_convey: That dividing top and bottom by cos9° gives (1 + tan9°)/(1 − tan9°), and that 1 is written as tan45°.
accept: divide top and bottom by cos nine to get one plus tan nine over one minus tan nine, and one is tan forty five
turn everything into tangents by dividing by cosine
write the one as tan forty five so the formula fits
cos nine tho divide cheste tan form vasthundi, one ante tan forty five
divide through and replace one by tan forty five

steps.why: Writing 1 as tan45° is not decoration — it is what makes the expression match the tan(A+B) formula exactly.
common_mistakes: Dividing by sin9° instead, which gives cotangents.

steps.label: Apply tan(A+B) and convert
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The formula gives tan54°, and 54° is 90° − 36° — so tan54° is cot36°.

recall.must_convey: That the expression is tan(45°+9°) = tan54°, and that tan54° = tan(90°−36°) = cot36°.
accept: it becomes tan fifty four which is tan of ninety minus thirty six equal to cot thirty six

steps.why: tan(90° − θ) = cot θ is what crosses between the two named functions. The question asked for cot, so that last conversion is required.
